acceptanceCriteria.statement: An isolated *-lab.html harness proves the multi-field carve-cube packing works BEFORE any production wiring: render the dendritic valley geometry into a HalfFloat RGBA cube carrying R=depth, G=mouth/apron, B=Strahler-order/width, read the channels back, and confirm the MAX-blend equation packs the extra channels correctly at confluences (deepest/highest-order/widest wins, no cross-channel corruption). Per feedback_isolated-test-harnesses: if the mechanism doesn't work in isolation, production can't save it.

verifyVia.input: Open the new packing harness on :9223; readback the cube G/B at known mouth nodes, headwater nodes, and a confluence; compare against the CPU-side graph values (mouth set, strahler, accum)
verifyVia.observable: G is nonzero only at/near real mouth nodes and zero on headwaters; B monotone with Strahler order; at a confluence each channel resolves to the max-correct value (no channel bleeds another's magnitude). Harness logs PASS for all probe points.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The router graph (receiver[], accum[], strahler[], isChannel[], isOcean[]), currently built in routeAndOrder and DISCARDED, is retained and used to bake two new fields into the existing carve cube: a mouth/apron field (G) at nodes where isChannel[i] && !isOcean[i] && isOcean[receiver[i]], sized by accum[]; and a Strahler-order/width field (B). buildValleyGeometry gains aMouth/aOrder vertex attributes and createCarveCubeMap's frag writes vec4(depth, mouth, order, 1). The shipped R=depth carve and its relief gate (uRiverCarveGateHi) are unchanged.
